# ringside assets

**Everything in this directory is generated** by `scripts/gen_ringside.py` and is regenerated by
`npm run assets`. Nothing here is vendored, downloaded, or derived from a third-party pack, so there
is nothing to attribute and nothing to license.

That is not the house pattern — `versus` and `beatemup` both resample CC0 packs through
`scripts/fighter_art.py`. It is procedural here because no usable source exists:

| source | why not |
|---|---|
| the vendored catalog (`assets/`, `scripts/asset_search`) | Ninja Adventure; no boxing art at all |
| `~/Downloads/versus-art` | LuizMelo Martial Hero 1/2/3, Medieval Warrior, ansimuz Mountain Dusk — **all side profile** |
| itch.io, free `boxing` tag | three 3D/voxel models, a music pack, one finished game. No 2D sprites |
| itch.io, paid | several 2D boxer packs, $1.99–$25, all side profile |
| OpenGameArt "Boxer Game Character" | **CC0**, and the only free 2D boxer found anywhere — side profile |

An over-the-shoulder boxing game needs a rear-view player and a front-facing opponent, which is the
one angle none of the above provides.

The only third-party input is the font, from the shared catalogue:

- `assets/fonts/kenney-high-square.ttf` — Kenney, CC0. Used for the banners and baked into
  `digits.png` via `fighter_art.digits_sheet`.

## Files

| file | scheme | cells |
|---|---|---|
| `opponent.png` | `sheet64:` | 28 — 14 upper-band poses x 2 bands |
| `opponent_lo.png` | `sheet6432:` | 10 — 5 lower-band poses x 2 bands |
| `player.png` | `sheet6432:` | 22 — 11 poses x 2 bands |
| `gloves.png` | `sheet32:` | 6 glove overlays |
| `spark.png` | `sheet32:` | 4 impact frames |
| `digits.png` | `sheet:` | 10 |
| `ring.png` | `background:` | 256x256, 9 colours |
| `preview-composite.png` | — | not shipped in the ROM; eight game situations at their real screen positions, so the art can be iterated without a build |

Every sheet holds **9 or fewer opaque colours**, well under the 15 that `clamp_colors` would
quantise at. That is why the fighter can be split across three PNGs without a colour step at the
waist seam: no quantisation ever runs, so the palettes are identical by construction rather than by
luck. `gen_ringside.py` keeps them that way by drawing only from one authored palette.
